[#1097](https://github.com/meocord/meocord/pull/1097) [`82f1144`](https://github.com/meocord/meocord/commit/82f11442156ea9e670b47ae28c8ff10f86279de6) Thanks [@l7aromeo](https://github.com/l7aromeo)! - When Discord refuses `@Defer`'s acknowledgement, or `respond(interaction).lock()`'s, because something else already answered the interaction (40060), the message is no longer locked. That other answer may be a reply, and the lock's two edits went to it: first the loading view with the message's controls disabled, then a copy of the message, so the reply's own content was lost. Now nothing edits it, and an error from the handler follows up privately as before.

A test that rejects `deferUpdate` with `createDiscordError(40060)` under `@Defer` now sees no `editReply` from the lock and its restore. Locking after the app's own `interaction.deferUpdate()` is unchanged.

[#1093](https://github.com/meocord/meocord/pull/1093) [`295ade3`](https://github.com/meocord/meocord/commit/295ade3ec4a3f0da32e058f520d7bfa3f9b48845) Thanks [@l7aromeo](https://github.com/l7aromeo)! - `meocord/eslint`'s packages are no longer listed in `meocord`'s `peerDependencies`. Listing them there made npm and Yarn 1 install the lint toolchain (about 115 packages) in production for a bot that lints with `meocord/eslint`, as every bot from `meocord create` does: `npm ci --omit=dev` installed it, and `npm audit --omit=dev` reported its advisories. They stay in `peerDependenciesMeta` as optional peers of any version, which pnpm, Bun and Yarn 2+ read as before. For `npm ci --omit=dev` to leave the toolchain out, update the bot's lockfile to this version with `npm install` or `npm update meocord`. Bun's production installs (`bun install --production`) still include the toolchain: Bun keeps an optional peer in a production install when the bot has it as a devDependency. `meocord/eslint` works as before. See [ESLint](/docs/4.3/eslint#adopting-it-by-hand).

[#1091](https://github.com/meocord/meocord/pull/1091) [`0e11e57`](https://github.com/meocord/meocord/commit/0e11e5769891ef3d544e5e817842843823780635) Thanks [@l7aromeo](https://github.com/l7aromeo)! - `meocord start --prod` and `meocord register` no longer load the bundler. A production install without optional dependencies, such as `npm ci --omit=dev --omit=optional`, can start the bot with `meocord start --prod`; before, it stopped with "Cannot find native binding". Without the bundler, `start --prod` also starts a little sooner and uses less memory, about 13 MB less on our test machine. The commands that build (`build`, `start` without `--prod`, `start --build`, `register --build`) still need the bundler and its native binding. See [Deployment](/docs/4.3/deployment#example).

[#1097](https://github.com/meocord/meocord/pull/1097) [`39630af`](https://github.com/meocord/meocord/commit/39630afbaca5bd233acd4184fcda91c72e2583ef) Thanks [@l7aromeo](https://github.com/l7aromeo)! - `respond(interaction).lock()` after the handler's own `interaction.deferReply()` no longer edits that deferred reply. The lock and the next `send()` used to turn the reply into a copy of the component's message, loading view and controls included, while the message itself stayed unlocked. Now the lock draws nothing once a reply or a deferred reply is the answer. After the handler's own `interaction.deferUpdate()` it locks the message as before.

For tests: a default-mode mock interaction's `ephemeral` now reads `null` after the mock's `update()` or `deferUpdate()`, or after a test marks the interaction `deferred` itself, as discord.js does, where it read `false`, with a placeholder warning after the mock's own answers. A test asserting `toBe(false)` there now fails; `toBeFalsy()` still passes. This is an exception to default mocks staying as they were: `lock()` reads `ephemeral` to tell an update from a reply, so the mock has to read as discord.js does for a test to see the lock it would see in production. Before any answer, after `reply()` or `deferReply()`, and with `useStrictMocks()`, nothing changes.

[#1089](https://github.com/meocord/meocord/pull/1089) [`411759c`](https://github.com/meocord/meocord/commit/411759c5d2382efb667a0f39eee93280e75252eb) Thanks [@l7aromeo](https://github.com/l7aromeo)! - A call is themed for the server its event names when the server is given as itself, after another value, or as the new value of an update whose old value was not cached. `@On` and `@Once` handlers for `guildCreate`, `guildUpdate`, `guildDelete` and the other events given a `Guild`, events given a server or a channel after a collection (`guildMembersChunk`, `messageDeleteBulk`, …), `threadMemberUpdate`, poll votes, and updates such as `presenceUpdate` with no cached old value now get `themeFor.guild`'s theme, as do functions `bindTheme` wraps when called with them. Before, they ran with no server's theme, and a bound function kept the theme of the call that bound it. A value from a direct message names no server, whether its `guildId` or its message's `guildId` is `null` or it is a direct message's channel or poll, so a later argument does not theme the call. See [Theming](/docs/4.3/theming#collectors-and-listeners).

An update whose old value was not cached also gets its new value's user, as it does when the old value is cached: a `presenceUpdate` is themed for its user's `themeFor.user` theme. Poll votes now also get the voter's `themeFor.user` theme. `voiceStateUpdate` and `voiceChannelEffectSend` now get their user's theme, and `autoModerationActionExecution`, `presenceUpdate` and `threadMemberUpdate` get it even when discord.js has not cached that user. `entitlementCreate`, `entitlementUpdate` and `entitlementDelete` get the entitlement's user, `subscriptionCreate`, `subscriptionUpdate` and `subscriptionDelete` the subscriber's, and `guildAuditLogEntryCreate` the executor's unless the bot took the action.

A creator is a call's user only in the event that created it: `stickerCreate`, `emojiCreate`, `guildSoundboardSoundCreate`, `threadCreate` for a newly created thread, `autoModerationRuleCreate`, `guildScheduledEventCreate` and `inviteCreate` get the creator's `themeFor.user` theme. Their update and delete events, and functions `bindTheme` wraps when called with the same values, get no user's theme. Before, `stickerUpdate`, `stickerDelete`, `emojiUpdate`, `emojiDelete`, `guildSoundboardSoundUpdate` and `guildSoundboardSoundDelete` were themed for the creator, as were bound functions given a sticker, an emoji or a sound.

`clientReady` and `ready` handlers, given the client, are no longer themed for the bot as a user.
